svg.title: The source picks f, the medium picks v, and λ has no say
svg.desc: Top left: a transverse wave labelled with crest, trough, amplitude and wavelength, above a longitudinal wave shown as alternating compressions and rarefactions. Top right: what each property is set by, and what happens when a wave crosses into a new medium — frequency unchanged, speed set by the new medium, wavelength following from v = f lambda. Bottom left: standing wave harmonics for a string or open pipe, where every harmonic is allowed and the fundamental wavelength is twice the length, against a closed pipe, where only odd harmonics fit and the fundamental wavelength is four times the length. Bottom right: the numbers to carry.
svg.text: The source picks f, the medium picks v, and λ has no say
v = fλ — so crossing into a new medium changes λ, never the frequency
longitudinal (sound): the same wave, drawn as density
A sets energy (E ∝ A²); f sets pitch and colour
f stays • v changes • λ follows: λ₂ = λ₁ · v₂/v₁
Beats: |f₁ − f₂| • constructive ΔL = nλ • destructive ΔL = (n + ½)λ
Doppler: approaching raises the pitch, receding lowers it — f_obs = f(v + v_o)/(v − v_s)
Sound is longitudinal and needs a medium; light is transverse and does not
